P62F-PC-L-061.stem: Refer to the graph. What is the correct order for analyzing the firm’s output and economic profit?

choices.A: Use P=MC on rising MC to find Q1, then measure P−ATC at Q1
choices.B: Choose the minimum ATC output first
choices.C: Use market quantity as firm output
choices.D: Measure profit before selecting output

P62F-PC-L-061.correct_answer: Use P=MC on rising MC to find Q1, then measure P−ATC at Q1
P62F-PC-L-061.feedback: The horizontal price line is also MR. Its intersection with rising MC selects Q1; only then can the price–ATC gap at Q1 establish per-unit profit.

P62F-PC-L-062.stem: Refer to the graph. What does the vertical gap between the price line and ATC at Q1 measure?

choices.A: Total economic profit
choices.B: Economic profit per unit
choices.C: Producer surplus for the whole market
choices.D: Marginal revenue minus marginal cost at every output

P62F-PC-L-062.feedback: Price and ATC are both dollars per unit, so their vertical difference is economic profit per unit. Multiplying that gap by Q1 would give total profit.

P62F-PC-L-063.stem: Refer to the graph. The price line touches minimum ATC at the selected output. What follows?

choices.A: The firm must exit
choices.B: Accounting profit must be zero
choices.C: The firm earns zero economic profit while covering normal profit
choices.D: The firm is below shutdown price

P62F-PC-L-063.correct_answer: The firm earns zero economic profit while covering normal profit
P62F-PC-L-063.feedback: At the selected output P=ATC, so total revenue equals total economic cost. Implicit owner returns are included in that cost, making zero economic profit compatible with normal profit.

P62F-PC-L-064.stem: Refer to the graph. Price lies below ATC but above AVC at the rising-MC output. What is the short-run decision?

choices.A: Shut down and eliminate fixed cost
choices.B: Produce at minimum ATC instead
choices.C: Raise price to ATC
choices.D: Produce and incur an economic loss

P62F-PC-L-064.correct_answer: Produce and incur an economic loss
P62F-PC-L-064.feedback: P above AVC means production covers variable cost and contributes toward unavoidable fixed cost. P below ATC means that contribution does not cover all fixed cost, so operating still incurs an economic loss.

P62F-PC-L-065.stem: Refer to the loss-making firm graph. Assume all firms are initially identical, fixed costs cannot be avoided this period, and input prices and cost curves stay unchanged as firms leave. Which sequence correctly separates present operation from eventual adjustment?

choices.A: The firm operates because P exceeds AVC; persistent losses induce exit; market supply falls and survivors’ MR and output rise until losses disappear
choices.B: The firm shuts down solely because P is below ATC; shutdown immediately removes all fixed costs and eliminates losses
choices.C: Losses induce entry; market supply rises and each survivor’s horizontal MR rises until zero profit
choices.D: Survivors raise their own selling prices first; their downward-sloping demand curves then shift right

P62F-PC-L-065.correct_answer: The firm operates because P exceeds AVC; persistent losses induce exit; market supply falls and survivors’ MR and output rise until losses disappear
P62F-PC-L-065.feedback: The displayed price lies between AVC and ATC, so production covers variable cost and some unavoidable fixed cost. Persistent economic losses discourage renewal and induce exit. Reduced market supply raises price and each survivor’s horizontal MR; output rises along unchanged rising MC until the standard long-run zero-profit condition is restored.

P62F-PC-L-066.stem: Refer to the graph. Price is below minimum AVC. Which conclusion is correct?

choices.A: The firm produces where price meets MC
choices.B: The firm supplies zero in the short run and bears fixed cost
choices.C: The firm breaks even
choices.D: The firm raises the market price

P62F-PC-L-066.correct_answer: The firm supplies zero in the short run and bears fixed cost
P62F-PC-L-066.feedback: Price below minimum AVC cannot cover variable cost at any positive output. Shutdown avoids variable cost but leaves unavoidable short-run fixed cost.

P62F-PC-L-067.stem: Refer to the graph. Which segment traces the price-taking firm’s short-run supply?

choices.A: The entire MC curve
choices.B: The AVC curve
choices.C: The rising MC segment at and above minimum AVC
choices.D: The falling portion of MC below AVC

P62F-PC-L-067.correct_answer: The rising MC segment at and above minimum AVC
P62F-PC-L-067.feedback: Above minimum AVC, each price selects the quantity where the rising MC curve equals that price. Below the shutdown threshold the firm supplies zero, so the entire MC curve is not supply.

P62F-PC-L-068.stem: Refer to the graph. How should information move from the market panel to the firm panel?

choices.A: The firm panel determines market price
choices.B: Market quantity becomes firm quantity
choices.C: The firm chooses P1 and the market chooses its output
choices.D: Market supply and demand determine P1; the firm uses P1 as MR to choose its own quantity

P62F-PC-L-068.correct_answer: Market supply and demand determine P1; the firm uses P1 as MR to choose its own quantity
P62F-PC-L-068.feedback: The market panel determines P1 from market supply and demand. The individual price taker faces that price as a horizontal MR line and uses its own MC to select firm output, not market quantity.

P62F-PC-L-069.stem: Refer to the graph. The initial firm price produces economic profit. What explains the market-supply shift shown?

choices.A: Entry by firms attracted by the profit
choices.B: Exit by loss-making firms
choices.C: A single firm cutting price
choices.D: A fall in market demand

P62F-PC-L-069.correct_answer: Entry by firms attracted by the profit
P62F-PC-L-069.feedback: Economic profit attracts entrants, adding output at each market price. The rightward supply shift lowers price and erodes incumbent profit.

P62F-PC-L-070.stem: Refer to the graph. The initial firm price produces an economic loss. What explains the market-supply shift shown?

choices.A: Entry expands supply and raises the survivors’ market price
choices.B: Exit reduces supply and raises the survivors’ market price
choices.C: Exit expands supply and lowers the survivors’ market price
choices.D: Entry reduces supply and lowers the survivors’ market price

P62F-PC-L-070.correct_answer: Exit reduces supply and raises the survivors’ market price
P62F-PC-L-070.feedback: Economic losses induce exit over time. Fewer firms shift market supply left; with demand fixed, price rises for surviving firms and their losses diminish.

P62F-PC-L-071.stem: Refer to the graph. What does the horizontal long-run industry supply curve imply?

choices.A: Each firm has horizontal MC
choices.B: Demand is perfectly elastic for the market
choices.C: Industry expansion does not change firms’ minimum long-run average cost
choices.D: Economic profit remains positive

P62F-PC-L-071.correct_answer: Industry expansion does not change firms’ minimum long-run average cost
P62F-PC-L-071.feedback: A horizontal long-run industry supply means additional industry output can be produced at the same minimum unit cost. It does not imply each individual firm has horizontal MC.

P62F-PC-L-072.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does this long-run industry supply curve slope upward?

choices.A: Individual firms set higher prices
choices.B: Marginal revenue slopes upward
choices.C: Entry permanently increases economic profit
choices.D: Industry expansion raises input costs or other firm costs

P62F-PC-L-072.correct_answer: Industry expansion raises input costs or other firm costs
P62F-PC-L-072.feedback: Expansion bids up inputs or otherwise raises firms’ costs. The higher long-run break-even cost requires a higher price to support the larger industry output.

P62F-PC-L-073.stem: Refer to the graph. What can produce the downward-sloping long-run industry supply shown?

choices.A: External economies that lower firm costs as the industry expands
choices.B: Rising input prices
choices.C: A downward-sloping individual firm demand curve
choices.D: A shutdown price above ATC

P62F-PC-L-073.correct_answer: External economies that lower firm costs as the industry expands
P62F-PC-L-073.feedback: External economies from industry expansion lower firms’ costs, permitting a lower break-even price at a larger industry output. Rising input prices would have the opposite effect.

P62F-PC-L-074.stem: Refer to the graph. At the long-run benchmark, which two conditions hold?

choices.A: P=AVC and economic profit is positive
choices.B: P=MC and P=minimum ATC
choices.C: P>MC and P>ATC
choices.D: MC is below AVC

P62F-PC-L-074.feedback: At the depicted benchmark P=MC matches marginal value with marginal cost, while P=minimum ATC covers total economic cost at its minimum. These establish allocative and productive efficiency respectively.

P62F-PC-L-075.stem: Refer to the graph. For the increasing-cost industry shown, how does the new long-run price compare with the original after demand rises?

choices.A: It returns exactly to the original price
choices.B: It falls below the original price
choices.C: It remains above the original price but below the short-run peak
choices.D: It remains at the short-run peak forever

P62F-PC-L-075.correct_answer: It remains above the original price but below the short-run peak
P62F-PC-L-075.feedback: Higher demand first raises price and creates profit. Entry then expands supply and lowers price from that peak, but industry expansion raises input costs, so the new long-run break-even price remains above the original.

P62F-PC-L-091.stem: Refer to the graph. Which sequence correctly extracts the firm’s economic profit from the graph?

choices.A: Choose minimum ATC first; multiply that output by the $30 market price to obtain economic profit
choices.B: Use AVC = $10 as profit per unit; multiply $10 by Q = 50 to obtain total profit
choices.C: Use rising-MC P = MC to get Q = 50; read ATC = $20; compute ($30 − $20) × 50
choices.D: Use market price $30 as profit per unit; multiply it by Q = 50 without subtracting cost

P62F-PC-L-091.correct_answer: Use rising-MC P = MC to get Q = 50; read ATC = $20; compute ($30 − $20) × 50
P62F-PC-L-091.feedback: Competitive-firm analysis chooses Q from P = MC first, then measures P − ATC at that quantity.

P62F-PC-L-092.stem: Refer to the graph. At the selected output, compare price with ATC. Which statement about economic profit is most accurate?

choices.A: The firm necessarily earns zero accounting profit because economic and accounting costs are identical
choices.B: The firm should shut down because any zero-profit outcome fails to cover average variable cost
choices.C: The firm bears a loss equal to total fixed cost because price only covers its variable cost
choices.D: The firm earns zero economic profit while covering the normal return included in economic cost

P62F-PC-L-092.correct_answer: The firm earns zero economic profit while covering the normal return included in economic cost
P62F-PC-L-092.feedback: Economic cost includes opportunity cost, so zero economic profit is consistent with normal profit.

P62F-PC-L-093.stem: Refer to the graph. If market price fell slightly below $25 but remained above AVC, with the cost curves unchanged, what would the firm do in the short run?

choices.A: Choose the lower-price rising-MC intersection and operate with a loss as long as price remains above AVC
choices.B: Shut down immediately because any price below ATC makes short-run production economically irrational for the displayed firm
choices.C: Keep Q fixed at 50 because price-taking firms never change output when the market price changes
choices.D: Raise the firm’s own price back to $25 and continue producing at the original break-even output

P62F-PC-L-093.correct_answer: Choose the lower-price rising-MC intersection and operate with a loss as long as price remains above AVC
P62F-PC-L-093.feedback: A competitive firm continues producing when price covers AVC, even if price is below ATC.

P62F-PC-L-094.stem: Refer to the graph. Trace the firm’s short-run and long-run logic in the loss case. Which sequence is valid?

choices.A: Choose Q = 30 where P = MC; because AVC < P < ATC, operate with a $300 loss and face exit pressure if it persists
choices.B: Choose minimum ATC; because P equals ATC there, operate with zero profit and no exit pressure for the displayed firm
choices.C: Shut down at Q = 0; because P < ATC, avoid all variable and fixed costs immediately
choices.D: Raise price to $40; keep Q = 30 and convert the displayed loss into economic profit

P62F-PC-L-094.correct_answer: Choose Q = 30 where P = MC; because AVC < P < ATC, operate with a $300 loss and face exit pressure if it persists
P62F-PC-L-094.feedback: The firm covers variable cost but not total cost, so it operates in the short run and may exit in the long run.

P62F-PC-L-095.stem: Refer to the graph. The $10 price line can intersect MC at a low-output portion of the curve. Why is that intersection not the firm’s chosen output?

choices.A: The firm must always choose the highest feasible output, so any low-output MC crossing is irrelevant
choices.B: ATC must fall to zero before a firm can produce, so the low-output crossing cannot be used
choices.C: A competitive firm ignores marginal cost at low output and chooses quantity from average total cost instead
choices.D: P is below minimum AVC, so the shutdown condition rules out the low-output P = MC crossing

P62F-PC-L-095.correct_answer: P is below minimum AVC, so the shutdown condition rules out the low-output P = MC crossing
P62F-PC-L-095.feedback: P = MC is not sufficient; the chosen point must also satisfy the shutdown condition and lie on rising MC.

P62F-PC-L-096.stem: Refer to the graph. If price were exactly $20 at point A, which statement would be correct?

choices.A: The firm is indifferent between producing at the shutdown output and shutting down in the short run
choices.B: The firm earns positive economic profit because price equals the minimum of average variable cost for the displayed firm
choices.C: The firm must exit immediately because reaching minimum AVC makes long-run production impossible
choices.D: The firm instead produces at point C because ATC determines the short-run shutdown quantity

P62F-PC-L-096.correct_answer: The firm is indifferent between producing at the shutdown output and shutting down in the short run
P62F-PC-L-096.feedback: At minimum AVC, revenue exactly covers variable cost, making the firm indifferent in the short run.

P62F-PC-L-097.stem: Refer to the graph. Which chain correctly describes the adjustment implied by the two panels?

choices.A: Market sets P = $40; firm chooses Q = 90; profit attracts entry; supply rises; price and firm output fall
choices.B: Firm chooses P = $40; market adopts Q = 90; losses cause exit; supply rises and price falls
choices.C: Market sets Q = 90 for every firm; entry occurs but leaves both market price and firm output unchanged for the displayed firm
choices.D: Firm chooses minimum AVC; entry shifts market demand right and raises both price and individual output

P62F-PC-L-097.correct_answer: Market sets P = $40; firm chooses Q = 90; profit attracts entry; supply rises; price and firm output fall
P62F-PC-L-097.feedback: The market determines price, the firm chooses output, and persistent profit triggers entry and lower price.

P62F-PC-L-099.stem: Refer to the graph. Trace the paired market-and-firm loss case through long-run adjustment. Which sequence is valid?

choices.A: Market sets P = $15; firm shuts down because P < ATC; persistent shutdown attracts entry and lowers price for the displayed firm
choices.B: Firm sets P = $15; market adopts Q = 50; persistent profit causes entry and higher market supply
choices.C: Market sets firm ATC at $18; firm shifts market demand left until price equals average cost
choices.D: Market sets P = $15; firm chooses Q = 50; AVC < P < ATC creates a loss; persistent loss causes exit and higher price

P62F-PC-L-099.correct_answer: Market sets P = $15; firm chooses Q = 50; AVC < P < ATC creates a loss; persistent loss causes exit and higher price
P62F-PC-L-099.feedback: The firm operates in the short run because P > AVC, but persistent loss creates exit pressure.

P62F-PC-LB-013.stem: Use the market and representative-firm panels. An analyst assigns the market’s total quantity to each firm and recommends producing at minimum ATC whenever that differs from the MR=MC quantity. Which correction preserves both the market-firm distinction and the operating decision?

choices.A: Divide market price by the number of firms, assign market quantity to each firm, and use ATC alone to decide shutdown.
choices.B: Take price from the market, but choose minimum ATC before considering MR; firms can then sell any desired amount at that cost.
choices.C: Take price from the market, choose each operating firm’s output on rising MC at that price, and check AVC before production and ATC for profit.
choices.D: Take the firm’s MC as the market demand curve, choose market quantity there, and ignore AVC if revenue is positive.

P62F-PC-LB-013.correct_answer: Take price from the market, choose each operating firm’s output on rising MC at that price, and check AVC before production and ATC for profit.
P62F-PC-LB-013.feedback: Market quantity is the sum of firms’ outputs, not the output of each firm. A price taker has MR=P; the candidate output satisfies rising MC=P when operating. AVC governs shutdown, while ATC determines economic profit.

P62F-PC-LB-015.stem: The graph initially shows P above ATC at Q1. An unavoidable fee for the current year raises fixed cost by more than the initial total profit, leaving demand, MC and AVC unchanged. The fee is avoidable by leaving before next year. Which sequence is correct?

choices.A: Keep the same short-run output but incur a loss; if these conditions persist, exit can avoid the future fee.
choices.B: Reduce short-run output because the fee raises MC; continue permanently because P still covers AVC.
choices.C: Keep the same short-run output and profit because a fixed fee never affects profit.
choices.D: Shut down immediately and avoid this year’s fee; reenter next year if P remains above AVC.

P62F-PC-LB-015.correct_answer: Keep the same short-run output but incur a loss; if these conditions persist, exit can avoid the future fee.
P62F-PC-LB-015.feedback: The fee does not change the MR=MC output or the current operating margin over variable cost. It does reduce profit, possibly below zero. A fee unavoidable now but avoidable next year separates short-run operation from long-run exit.

P62F-PC-LB-016.stem: The graph shows AVC<P<ATC at the operating quantity Q1. Fixed cost is unavoidable this period. A student says shutting down removes the entire loss (ATC−P)Q1. Which comparison correctly evaluates production versus shutdown?

choices.A: Producing incurs (ATC−P)Q1, while shutdown loses zero because all costs become avoidable immediately.
choices.B: Producing incurs (ATC−P)Q1, while shutdown loses all fixed cost; producing covers (P−AVC)Q1 of that fixed cost and is preferable now.
choices.C: Producing covers no fixed cost because P<ATC, so shutdown and production necessarily have identical losses.
choices.D: Producing earns positive economic profit because P>AVC, so the stated loss rectangle should be ignored.

P62F-PC-LB-016.correct_answer: Producing incurs (ATC−P)Q1, while shutdown loses all fixed cost; producing covers (P−AVC)Q1 of that fixed cost and is preferable now.
P62F-PC-LB-016.feedback: Revenue exceeds variable cost, so production contributes a positive amount toward unavoidable fixed cost. The operating loss is smaller than the fixed-cost loss under shutdown, although persistent losses can still lead to long-run exit.

P62F-PC-LB-017.stem: The graph shows a firm below its AVC shutdown threshold. Compare an unconditional lump-sum grant with a per-unit subsidy large enough to raise the firm’s net receipt above that threshold. Fixed cost is unavoidable this period. Which operating comparison is correct?

choices.A: Both policies change marginal receipts equally, so either grant necessarily restores production.
choices.B: The lump-sum grant lowers MC and restores production, while the per-unit subsidy affects fixed cost only.
choices.C: The lump-sum grant alone leaves the shutdown decision unchanged; the per-unit subsidy changes marginal receipts and can make production worthwhile.
choices.D: Neither policy can change production because any firm with an initial loss must shut down forever.

P62F-PC-LB-017.correct_answer: The lump-sum grant alone leaves the shutdown decision unchanged; the per-unit subsidy changes marginal receipts and can make production worthwhile.
P62F-PC-LB-017.feedback: An unconditional grant does not change the payoff difference between producing and not producing. A per-unit subsidy is earned only on output and changes the net price compared with MC and AVC, potentially crossing the operating threshold.

P62F-PC-LB-018.stem: Use the short-run supply graph. Compare a rise in unavoidable fixed rent with a rise in the variable cost of every unit produced, holding market demand unchanged. Which statement separates the two effects on firm supply?

choices.A: Both costs shift short-run supply upward by the same amount because both increase ATC.
choices.B: The fixed rent shifts short-run supply upward, while higher variable cost affects only long-run exit.
choices.C: Neither cost affects supply until entry occurs because a price-taking firm cannot change output.
choices.D: The fixed rent alone leaves MC and AVC, and thus short-run supply, unchanged; higher variable cost can raise MC and the shutdown threshold.

P62F-PC-LB-018.correct_answer: The fixed rent alone leaves MC and AVC, and thus short-run supply, unchanged; higher variable cost can raise MC and the shutdown threshold.
P62F-PC-LB-018.feedback: The operating supply relation uses rising MC above minimum AVC. Fixed rent does not enter either marginal or variable cost, although it affects profit and later exit. Variable-cost changes directly affect the operating comparison.

P62F-PC-M-032.stem: Refer to the graph. At the 50-unit output, what vertical price–ATC gap represents profit on each unit?

choices.A: $10 per unit
choices.B: $20 per unit
choices.C: $30 per unit
choices.D: $40 per unit

P62F-PC-M-032.feedback: Profit per unit is P − ATC = $30 − $20 = $10.

P62F-PC-M-036.stem: Refer to the graph. The blue ATC guide at the chosen 30-unit output lands on which dollar value?
P62F-PC-M-036.feedback: The ATC guide at Q = 30 is $40.

P62F-PC-M-037.stem: Refer to the graph. The green AVC marker at Q = 30 gives what variable cost per unit?
P62F-PC-M-037.feedback: The AVC guide at Q = 30 is $20.

P62F-PC-M-040.stem: Refer to the graph. Where does the firm’s short-run supply curve begin?

choices.A: At the left end of the entire MC curve
choices.B: At point C and then along ATC
choices.C: At point A and then along rising MC
choices.D: Along the AVC curve below A

P62F-PC-M-040.correct_answer: At point A and then along rising MC
P62F-PC-M-040.feedback: Short-run supply is rising MC at and above minimum AVC.

P62F-PC-M-041.stem: Refer to the graph. At the 90-unit output in the paired profit graph, what vertical price–ATC gap represents profit per unit?

choices.A: $20 per unit
choices.B: $5 per unit
choices.C: $15 per unit
choices.D: $40 per unit

P62F-PC-M-041.feedback: Price is $40 and ATC is $20, so profit per unit is $20.

P62F-PC-M-043.stem: Refer to the graph. How does the market-panel equilibrium price enter the representative firm’s decision?

choices.A: It becomes the firm’s ATC curve, determining average cost at every possible output level
choices.B: It becomes the firm’s quantity of 75, so market quantity and individual output are identical
choices.C: It becomes the firm’s horizontal P = MR = AR line used to choose output along MC
choices.D: It shifts the firm’s MC curve upward, changing production cost without changing marginal revenue

P62F-PC-M-043.correct_answer: It becomes the firm’s horizontal P = MR = AR line used to choose output along MC
P62F-PC-M-043.feedback: A price-taking firm accepts the market price as its marginal and average revenue.

P62F-PC-M-046.stem: Refer to the graph. Use price and AVC at the chosen output. Why does the representative firm continue producing in the short run?

choices.A: P = $15 exceeds AVC = $10 at Q = 50, so revenue covers variable cost and part of fixed cost
choices.B: P = $15 exceeds ATC = $18 at Q = 50, so the firm is earning positive economic profit
choices.C: The competitive firm can raise its own price above $15, so it avoids the loss shown by ATC
choices.D: Producing at Q = 50 eliminates fixed cost, so any price above AVC guarantees zero economic loss

P62F-PC-M-046.correct_answer: P = $15 exceeds AVC = $10 at Q = 50, so revenue covers variable cost and part of fixed cost
P62F-PC-M-046.feedback: The firm covers variable cost and part of fixed cost because P > AVC.

P62F-PC-M-047.stem: Refer to the graph. What economic profit does the representative firm earn at the long-run equilibrium?
P62F-PC-M-047.feedback: Price equals ATC at the selected output, so economic profit is zero.

P62F-PC-M-048.stem: Refer to the graph. Which pair of conditions holds at the representative firm’s selected output?

choices.A: P < AVC and MC < ATC for the displayed firm
choices.B: P = MC and P = minimum ATC
choices.C: P > ATC and MC < AVC
choices.D: P = AVC and ATC = 0

P62F-PC-M-048.correct_answer: P = MC and P = minimum ATC
P62F-PC-M-048.feedback: Long-run competitive equilibrium has P = MC and P at minimum ATC.

P62G-MON-B2-020.stem: At Granite Utility’s optimum, P=$61.90, ATC=$35.03, AVC=$21.90, and Q=19.05. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with ATC
choices.B: Price compared with AVC
choices.C: MR compared with demand
choices.D: Fixed cost compared with total revenue

P62G-MON-B2-020.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B2-023.stem: At Harbor Software’s optimum, P=$68.59, ATC=$68.05, AVC=$24.59, and Q=20.71. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with AVC
choices.B: Price compared with ATC
choices.C: MR compared with demand
choices.D: Fixed cost compared with total revenue

P62G-MON-B2-023.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B2-026.stem: At Iron Gate Rail’s optimum, P=$58.87, ATC=$57.18, AVC=$21.87, and Q=22.09. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with ATC
choices.B: MR compared with demand
choices.C: Fixed cost compared with total revenue
choices.D: Price compared with AVC

P62G-MON-B2-026.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B2-029.stem: At Juniper Licensing’s optimum, P=$73.85, ATC=$48.60, AVC=$25.85, and Q=18.46. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with ATC
choices.B: MR compared with demand
choices.C: Price compared with AVC
choices.D: Fixed cost compared with total revenue

P62G-MON-B2-029.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B2-032.stem: At Keystone Media’s optimum, P=$56.32, ATC=$118.63, AVC=$48.32, and Q=4.27. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with ATC
choices.B: Price compared with AVC
choices.C: MR compared with demand
choices.D: Fixed cost compared with total revenue

P62G-MON-B2-032.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B2-035.stem: At Lakeside Network’s optimum, P=$64.40, ATC=$54.52, AVC=$20.90, and Q=19.33. Which comparison controls shutdown?

choices.A: Price compared with AVC
choices.B: Price compared with ATC
choices.C: MR compared with demand
choices.D: Fixed cost compared with total revenue

P62G-MON-B2-035.feedback: The shutdown threshold is average variable cost.

P62G-MON-B3-057.stem: Refer to the graph. Which comparison best captures the unregulated monopoly outcome and the allocatively efficient outcome?

choices.A: Unregulated: Q = 90, P = $20; efficient: Q = 45, P = $47
choices.B: Unregulated: Q = 45, P = $47; efficient D = MC: Q = 90, P = $20
choices.C: Unregulated: Q = 45, P = $20; efficient: Q = 90, P = $47
choices.D: Both outcomes occur at Q = 45 because MC is horizontal

P62G-MON-B3-057.correct_answer: Unregulated: Q = 45, P = $47; efficient D = MC: Q = 90, P = $20
P62G-MON-B3-057.feedback: MR = MC determines the unregulated monopoly output, while D = MC identifies the allocatively efficient benchmark.

P62G-MON-B3-058.stem: Refer to the graph. Which statement correctly contrasts fair-return pricing with marginal-cost pricing?

choices.A: Fair-return sets P = MC at Q = 140; MC pricing sets P = ATC near Q = 116
choices.B: Both rules preserve the unregulated price near $27 and leave output close to Q = 70
choices.C: MC pricing produces less output than fair-return pricing because the MC curve is horizontal
choices.D: Fair-return covers ATC near Q = 116; MC pricing reaches Q = 140 but P < ATC

P62G-MON-B3-058.correct_answer: Fair-return covers ATC near Q = 116; MC pricing reaches Q = 140 but P < ATC
P62G-MON-B3-058.feedback: The graph shows the classic tradeoff: average-cost pricing supports break-even, while marginal-cost pricing reaches the efficient quantity but may require a subsidy.

P62G-MON-EL-001.stem: A monopolist has demand P=108−2Q, MC=20+0.25Q, and fixed cost $300. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-001.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-003.stem: A monopolist has demand P=120−2.5Q, MC=24+0.2Q, and fixed cost $420. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-003.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-005.stem: A monopolist has demand P=96−1.6Q, MC=18+0.35Q, and fixed cost $350. Which paired result is correct?

choices.A: Q=40 and P=$32

P62G-MON-EL-005.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-007.stem: A monopolist has demand P=112−2.2Q, MC=22+0.3Q, and fixed cost $500. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-007.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-009.stem: A monopolist has demand P=100−2Q, MC=20+0.2Q, and fixed cost $850. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-009.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-011.stem: A monopolist has demand P=92−1.5Q, MC=18+0.35Q, and fixed cost $780. Which paired result is correct?

choices.B: Q=40 and P=$32

P62G-MON-EL-011.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-013.stem: A monopolist has demand P=116−2.4Q, MC=26+0.25Q, and fixed cost $900. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-013.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-015.stem: A monopolist has demand P=105−2.1Q, MC=18+0.3Q, and fixed cost $650. Which paired result is correct?
P62G-MON-EL-015.feedback: Set MR=MC for Q and substitute Q into demand for P.

P62G-MON-EL-031.stem: Refer to the graph. Suppose fixed cost rises by $360 while demand, MR, and MC remain unchanged. What happens to the monopoly choice and economic profit?

choices.A: Q and P stay at 36 and $42; profit falls from $540 to $180
choices.B: Q falls to 24 and P rises to $48; profit stays $540
choices.C: Q rises to 60 and P falls to $30; profit becomes zero
choices.D: Q and P stay at 36 and $42; profit rises to $900

P62G-MON-EL-031.correct_answer: Q and P stay at 36 and $42; profit falls from $540 to $180
P62G-MON-EL-031.feedback: A fixed-cost change does not alter MR or MC, so Q and P stay put. Profit falls dollar-for-dollar by $360.

P62G-MON-EL-032.stem: Refer to the graph. Why would moving output from 36 toward the D = MC quantity of 60 reduce allocative inefficiency?

choices.A: MR exceeds price on every unit through Q = 60
choices.B: Demand exceeds MC on the additional units
choices.C: ATC is constant between Q = 36 and Q = 60
choices.D: The monopoly price stays fixed at $42 as output expands

P62G-MON-EL-032.correct_answer: Demand exceeds MC on the additional units
P62G-MON-EL-032.feedback: Between the monopoly quantity and D = MC, demand lies above MC, so mutually beneficial units are not produced under monopoly.

P62G-MON-EL-033.stem: Refer to the graph. If ATC at Q = 40 fell from $45 to $35 while demand, MR, and MC remained unchanged, what would result?

choices.A: The firm switches to Q = 67 and earns zero economic profit
choices.B: Price falls automatically from $40 to the new ATC of $35
choices.C: Q = 40 and P = $40 stay; the firm still loses $200
choices.D: Q = 40 and P = $40 stay; profit becomes $200

P62G-MON-EL-033.correct_answer: Q = 40 and P = $40 stay; profit becomes $200
P62G-MON-EL-033.feedback: The marginal decision is unchanged. Profit becomes ($40 − $35) × 40 = $200.

P62G-MON-EL-034.stem: Refer to the graph. What feature shows the allocative gap created by monopoly?

choices.A: Demand stays above MC between Q = 40 and Q ≈ 67
choices.B: MR stays above demand between Q = 40 and Q ≈ 67
choices.C: ATC stays below price at the monopoly quantity of 40
choices.D: MC is horizontal between the monopoly and benchmark outputs

P62G-MON-EL-034.correct_answer: Demand stays above MC between Q = 40 and Q ≈ 67
P62G-MON-EL-034.feedback: Units between the monopoly quantity and D = MC have marginal benefit above marginal cost but are not produced.

P62G-MON-EL-036.stem: Refer to the graph. Why can marginal-cost pricing create a financing problem for this natural monopoly?

choices.A: At Q = 90, MR is above the demand price
choices.B: At Q = 45, price is below marginal cost
choices.C: At Q = 90, ATC is above the $20 regulated price
choices.D: ATC rises sharply as output expands from 45 to 90

P62G-MON-EL-036.correct_answer: At Q = 90, ATC is above the $20 regulated price
P62G-MON-EL-036.feedback: With economies of scale, ATC can exceed MC at the efficient output, so P = MC may not cover total cost.

P62G-MON-EL-037.stem: Refer to the graph. Compared with the unregulated monopoly outcome, moving to D = MC would:

choices.A: Halve output from 90 to 45 and raise price from $20 to $47
choices.B: Keep output at 45 while cutting price to $20
choices.C: Raise output to 125 while leaving price at $47
choices.D: Double output from 45 to 90 and cut price from $47 to $20

P62G-MON-EL-037.correct_answer: Double output from 45 to 90 and cut price from $47 to $20
P62G-MON-EL-037.feedback: The marked outcomes are Q = 45, P = $47 for monopoly and Q = 90, P = $20 at D = MC.

P62G-MON-EL-038.stem: Refer to the graph. Which price-output ordering is consistent with the outcomes shown?

choices.A: Prices rise $10 → $16 → $27 as output rises 70 → 116 → 140
choices.B: Price stays $27 while output rises 70 → 140
choices.C: Prices fall $27 → $16 → $10 as output rises 70 → 116 → 140
choices.D: Output falls 140 → 70 as prices fall $27 → $10

P62G-MON-EL-038.feedback: Stronger regulation toward marginal-cost pricing lowers price and expands output in the displayed natural monopoly.

P62G-MON-EL-039.stem: Refer to the graph. Why is average-cost pricing less allocatively efficient than marginal-cost pricing?

choices.A: Fair-return leaves P < MC and Q above 140 units
choices.B: Average-cost pricing reaches D = MC and produces positive profit
choices.C: Average-cost pricing makes demand horizontal at the regulated price
choices.D: Fair-return leaves P > MC and Q below 140 units

P62G-MON-EL-039.correct_answer: Fair-return leaves P > MC and Q below 140 units
P62G-MON-EL-039.feedback: Fair-return pricing covers costs but stops short of the D = MC quantity because P remains above MC.

P62G-MON-EL-040.stem: Refer to the graph. Why might the regulator need a subsidy under marginal-cost pricing?

choices.A: P = $10 is below ATC = $15 at Q = 140
choices.B: P = $27 exceeds ATC at Q = 70
choices.C: P = $16 equals ATC at Q = 116
choices.D: MR is greater than demand at Q = 140

P62G-MON-EL-040.correct_answer: P = $10 is below ATC = $15 at Q = 140
P62G-MON-EL-040.feedback: At the efficient quantity, total revenue at P = MC does not cover average total cost.

P62G-MON-H-002.stem: Refer to the graph. Which comparison determines whether the monopolist earns economic profit at Q1?

choices.A: P1 compared with MC at Q1
choices.B: P1 compared with ATC at Q1
choices.C: MR compared with demand at Q1
choices.D: ATC compared with AVC at zero output

P62G-MON-H-002.correct_answer: P1 compared with ATC at Q1

P62G-MON-H-003.stem: Refer to the graph. At Q1, why is price greater than marginal revenue?

choices.A: Marginal cost includes fixed cost
choices.B: Demand is perfectly elastic
choices.C: Lowering price to sell Q1 creates a price effect on prior units
choices.D: Average revenue is below demand

P62G-MON-H-003.correct_answer: Lowering price to sell Q1 creates a price effect on prior units
P62G-MON-H-003.feedback: For single-price monopoly, MR reflects both the output and price effects.

P62G-MON-H-004.stem: Refer to the graph. Suppose fixed cost rises while demand, MR, and MC remain unchanged. What happens in the short run?

choices.A: Q1 falls and P1 rises
choices.B: Q1 rises and P1 falls
choices.C: The MR curve shifts downward
choices.D: Q1 and P1 remain unchanged, but profit falls

P62G-MON-H-004.correct_answer: Q1 and P1 remain unchanged, but profit falls
P62G-MON-H-004.feedback: Fixed cost shifts ATC but does not change the MR=MC output.

P62G-MON-H-005.stem: Refer to the graph. The demand price P1 currently lies above ATC at Q1. Suppose a higher fixed cost raises ATC exactly to P1 without changing demand, MR or MC. The monopoly would then earn:

choices.A: Zero economic profit while covering all opportunity costs
choices.B: Zero accounting profit necessarily
choices.C: A loss equal to fixed cost
choices.D: Positive profit because P1 exceeds MC

P62G-MON-H-005.correct_answer: Zero economic profit while covering all opportunity costs
P62G-MON-H-005.feedback: The higher fixed cost raises ATC without moving the MR = MC output or demand price. When ATC reaches P1 at Q1, revenue covers all economic costs and economic profit becomes zero. The original plotted curves need not already show tangency.

P62G-MON-H-006.stem: Refer to the graph. P1 is below ATC but above AVC at Q1. What should the monopolist do?

choices.A: Shut down because P1 is below ATC
choices.B: Produce Q1 and minimize its short-run loss
choices.C: Raise price without changing quantity
choices.D: Produce the competitive quantity

P62G-MON-H-006.correct_answer: Produce Q1 and minimize its short-run loss
P62G-MON-H-006.feedback: Covering AVC and part of fixed cost reduces the loss.

P62G-MON-H-007.stem: Refer to the graph. What is the monopolist’s total economic loss if the vertical gap between ATC and P1 is L?

choices.A: One-half of L multiplied by Q1
choices.B: The gap between P1 and MC multiplied by Q1
choices.C: L multiplied by Q1
choices.D: Fixed cost minus total revenue

P62G-MON-H-007.feedback: Loss is a rectangle: loss per unit times output.

P62G-MON-H-008.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does the MR = MC rule remain relevant even when the monopolist is taking an economic loss?

choices.A: It guarantees positive accounting profit
choices.B: It identifies the shutdown price directly
choices.C: It makes price equal marginal cost
choices.D: It identifies the output that minimizes the loss, provided price covers AVC

P62G-MON-H-008.correct_answer: It identifies the output that minimizes the loss, provided price covers AVC
P62G-MON-H-008.feedback: Marginal analysis chooses the best feasible output, not necessarily a profitable one.

P62G-MON-H-009.stem: Refer to the graph. The best available price is below AVC. What should the monopolist do in the short run?

choices.A: Produce zero in the short run
choices.B: Produce Q1 because MR=MC
choices.C: Produce where demand intersects MC
choices.D: Ignore AVC because it has market power

P62G-MON-H-009.correct_answer: Produce zero in the short run
P62G-MON-H-009.feedback: Price below AVC means revenue cannot cover avoidable cost.

P62G-MON-H-010.stem: Refer to the graph. After short-run shutdown, which cost remains?

choices.A: Variable cost of the unproduced units
choices.B: Fixed cost
choices.C: Marginal revenue
choices.D: The deadweight-loss triangle

P62G-MON-H-010.feedback: Shutdown avoids variable cost but not short-run fixed cost.

P62G-MON-H-011.stem: Refer to the graph. Q1 is monopoly output and Q2 is the D=MC quantity. The interval from Q1 to Q2 consists of units for which:

choices.A: Marginal revenue exceeds demand
choices.B: Average total cost is necessarily falling
choices.C: Buyer willingness to pay exceeds marginal cost
choices.D: Price discrimination is impossible

P62G-MON-H-011.correct_answer: Buyer willingness to pay exceeds marginal cost
P62G-MON-H-011.feedback: Those omitted units would add to total surplus.

P62G-MON-H-012.stem: Refer to the graph. Which area concept is created by restricting output from Q2 to Q1?

choices.A: A transfer equal to all monopoly profit
choices.B: Tariff revenue
choices.C: Fixed cost
choices.D: Deadweight loss from unrealized trades

P62G-MON-H-012.feedback: The restriction eliminates trades with positive net benefit.

P62G-MON-H-031.stem: Refer to the graph. At the profit-maximizing output, why is the price read from demand above marginal revenue?

choices.A: An extra sale requires lowering price on earlier units
choices.B: Marginal cost is already embedded in the downward demand curve
choices.C: Average total cost must exceed marginal revenue at every output
choices.D: The monopolist takes a fixed market price on all units sold

P62G-MON-H-031.correct_answer: An extra sale requires lowering price on earlier units
P62G-MON-H-031.feedback: For a downward-sloping demand curve, expanding sales lowers the price received on previous units, so MR lies below price.

P62G-MON-H-032.stem: Refer to the graph. Why would moving output from 36 toward 60 units reduce profit?

choices.A: Demand exceeds ATC over the entire interval
choices.B: Beyond Q = 36, MC exceeds MR
choices.C: Price becomes greater than marginal revenue
choices.D: ATC immediately becomes fixed cost

P62G-MON-H-032.feedback: Once output passes MR = MC, the additional units cost more at the margin than they add to revenue.

P62G-MON-H-034.stem: Refer to the graph. Which comparison correctly describes the monopoly outcome and the D = MC benchmark?

choices.A: Monopoly: P = $30, Q = 60; benchmark: P = $42, Q = 36
choices.B: Monopoly: P = $24, Q = 36; benchmark: P = $27, Q = 60
choices.C: Monopoly and the benchmark both have P = $30 and Q = 60
choices.D: Monopoly: P = $42, Q = 36; D = MC benchmark: P = $30, Q = 60

P62G-MON-H-034.correct_answer: Monopoly: P = $42, Q = 36; D = MC benchmark: P = $30, Q = 60
P62G-MON-H-034.feedback: The monopoly restricts output to 36 and charges $42; the D = MC benchmark is 60 units at $30.

P62G-MON-H-036.stem: Refer to the graph. Why is Q = 67 not the profit-maximizing monopoly output?

choices.A: At Q = 67, marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue
choices.B: At Q = 67, price is greater than marginal cost
choices.C: At Q = 67, ATC is necessarily zero
choices.D: The monopolist must always choose the demand intercept

P62G-MON-H-036.correct_answer: At Q = 67, marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue
P62G-MON-H-036.feedback: A monopolist maximizes profit where MR = MC, not where demand equals MC.

P62G-MON-H-041.stem: Refer to the graph. Which feature is consistent with a natural monopoly over the relevant range?

choices.A: ATC declines as output expands toward the efficient quantity
choices.B: MR is horizontal across the relevant output range
choices.C: Demand becomes perfectly elastic near the efficient output
choices.D: MC rises faster than demand throughout the relevant range

P62G-MON-H-041.correct_answer: ATC declines as output expands toward the efficient quantity
P62G-MON-H-041.feedback: Declining ATC over the relevant output range signals economies of scale that can support natural monopoly.

P62G-MON-H-043.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does the fair-return outcome near Q = 116 and P = $16 imply approximately zero economic profit?

choices.A: P = ATC at the fair-return output
choices.B: P = MR at the fair-return output
choices.C: MC = ATC at the $10 regulated price
choices.D: Total revenue equals zero near Q = 116

P62G-MON-H-043.correct_answer: P = ATC at the fair-return output
P62G-MON-H-043.feedback: Average-cost pricing sets P = ATC, covering economic costs without positive economic profit.

P62G-MON-L-093.stem: Refer to the graph. Which sequence best describes the monopoly outcome shown?

choices.A: D = MC gives Q = 40; MR gives P = $20; P > ATC therefore creates economic profit
choices.B: MR = ATC gives Q = 67; demand gives P = $27; the monopolist therefore breaks even
choices.C: MR = MC gives Q = 40; demand gives P = $40; P < ATC causes a loss; D = MC is near Q = 67
choices.D: MC = ATC gives Q = 40; demand gives P = $45; economic profit is therefore zero

P62G-MON-L-093.correct_answer: MR = MC gives Q = 40; demand gives P = $40; P < ATC causes a loss; D = MC is near Q = 67
P62G-MON-L-093.feedback: The graph separates the monopoly marginal decision, price read from demand, loss test against ATC, and efficient D = MC benchmark.

P62G-MON-L-094.stem: Refer to the graph. What is the strongest reason a subsidy may be paired with marginal-cost pricing?

choices.A: At efficient output, P = MC remains below ATC
choices.B: At efficient output, P exceeds both MC and ATC
choices.C: At monopoly output, price is already below marginal cost
choices.D: A subsidy is needed to keep MR above demand at Q = 90

P62G-MON-L-094.correct_answer: At efficient output, P = MC remains below ATC
P62G-MON-L-094.feedback: A natural monopoly can be allocatively efficient at P = MC yet unable to cover total cost because ATC remains higher.

P62H-MCMP-B2-020.stem: As entry erodes short-run profit, what zero-profit geometry characterizes the standard long-run equilibrium?

choices.A: Demand is horizontal at minimum ATC
choices.B: Demand is tangent to ATC and economic profit is zero
choices.C: Price equals MC and ATC
choices.D: MR is tangent to demand

P62H-MCMP-B2-020.correct_answer: Demand is tangent to ATC and economic profit is zero
P62H-MCMP-B2-020.feedback: Entry or exit continues until P=ATC at the chosen output.

P62H-MCMP-B3-039.stem: Which welfare conclusion about Grove Coffee is safest?

choices.A: Compare added consumer value or information with resource cost and market-power effects
choices.B: All differentiation is wasteful
choices.C: All advertising raises total surplus
choices.D: Zero economic profit guarantees efficiency

P62H-MCMP-B3-039.feedback: Welfare requires a balanced comparison of benefits and costs.
