P62H-MCMP-B3-055.stem: Refer to the graph. The firm produces Q = 36 while efficient scale is Q = 50. Which conclusion best describes the long-run outcome?

choices.A: The firm has 14 units of excess capacity and positive economic profit
choices.B: The firm has 14 units of excess capacity while earning zero economic profit
choices.C: The firm is productively efficient because P equals ATC
choices.D: The firm is allocatively efficient because entry has occurred

P62H-MCMP-B3-055.correct_answer: The firm has 14 units of excess capacity while earning zero economic profit
P62H-MCMP-B3-055.feedback: The firm earns zero profit because P = ATC at Q = 36, but efficient scale is Q = 50, leaving 14 units of excess capacity.

P62H-MCMP-EL-016.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=20, minimum-ATC output Q2=34.64, price $70.00 and MC=$50.00. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $50.00; excess capacity 20 units.
choices.B: Markup $20.00; excess capacity 14.64 units.
choices.C: Markup $20.00; excess capacity 34.64 units.
choices.D: Markup $70.00; excess capacity 14.64 units.

P62H-MCMP-EL-016.feedback: Markup is P−MC=70.00−50.00=$20.00. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=34.64−20=14.64 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-017.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does the firm not expand from Q1 toward Q2 even though ATC would fall?

choices.A: The firm cannot physically produce beyond Q1 because excess capacity is a binding production limit
choices.B: Price would automatically equal MC
choices.C: Beyond Q1, marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue under its current demand
choices.D: Entry is legally prohibited

P62H-MCMP-EL-017.correct_answer: Beyond Q1, marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue under its current demand
P62H-MCMP-EL-017.feedback: Profit maximization, not minimum ATC alone, determines output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-018.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=24, minimum-ATC output Q2=42.93, price $76.00 and MC=$49.60. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $49.60; excess capacity 24 units.
choices.B: Markup $26.40; excess capacity 42.93 units.
choices.C: Markup $76.00; excess capacity 18.93 units.
choices.D: Markup $26.40; excess capacity 18.93 units.

P62H-MCMP-EL-018.feedback: Markup is P−MC=76.00−49.60=$26.40. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=42.93−24=18.93 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-020.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=18, minimum-ATC output Q2=30.12, price $64.00 and MC=$47.80. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $47.80; excess capacity 18 units.
choices.B: Markup $16.20; excess capacity 12.12 units.
choices.C: Markup $16.20; excess capacity 30.12 units.
choices.D: Markup $64.00; excess capacity 12.12 units.

P62H-MCMP-EL-020.feedback: Markup is P−MC=64.00−47.80=$16.20. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=30.12−18=12.12 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-021.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does P = ATC at Q1 not imply allocative efficiency?

choices.A: Price still exceeds marginal cost at Q1
choices.B: Price is below average variable cost at Q1
choices.C: Marginal revenue exceeds demand at Q1
choices.D: Output exceeds efficient scale at Q1

P62H-MCMP-EL-021.correct_answer: Price still exceeds marginal cost at Q1
P62H-MCMP-EL-021.feedback: P = ATC establishes zero economic profit, but allocative efficiency requires P = MC; the graph shows P > MC.

P62H-MCMP-EL-022.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=28, minimum-ATC output Q2=51.63, price $82.00 and MC=$48.40. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $48.40; excess capacity 28 units.
choices.B: Markup $33.60; excess capacity 51.63 units.
choices.C: Markup $82.00; excess capacity 23.63 units.
choices.D: Markup $33.60; excess capacity 23.63 units.

P62H-MCMP-EL-022.feedback: Markup is P−MC=82.00−48.40=$33.60. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=51.63−28=23.63 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-023.stem: Refer to the graph. If firms are earning short-run profit before reaching the long-run tangency shown, which effect of entry moves the market toward that outcome?

choices.A: Existing firms’ demand shifts left
choices.B: Existing firms’ marginal cost shifts right
choices.C: Industry demand becomes perfectly elastic
choices.D: The minimum point of ATC shifts to Q1

P62H-MCMP-EL-023.feedback: Entry adds substitutes and shifts the demand curve facing each existing firm left until it is tangent to ATC.

P62H-MCMP-EL-024.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=22, minimum-ATC output Q2=35.47, price $68.00 and MC=$50.40. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $50.40; excess capacity 22 units.
choices.B: Markup $17.60; excess capacity 13.47 units.
choices.C: Markup $17.60; excess capacity 35.47 units.
choices.D: Markup $68.00; excess capacity 13.47 units.

P62H-MCMP-EL-024.feedback: Markup is P−MC=68.00−50.40=$17.60. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=35.47−22=13.47 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-025.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does the firm retain a positive markup despite earning zero economic profit?

choices.A: Demand lies above marginal cost at Q1
choices.B: Demand is tangent to marginal cost at Q2
choices.C: Average total cost is vertical at Q1
choices.D: Marginal revenue equals demand at every output

P62H-MCMP-EL-025.correct_answer: Demand lies above marginal cost at Q1
P62H-MCMP-EL-025.feedback: The downward-sloping demand curve gives a price above marginal cost at Q1 even though tangency with ATC makes economic profit zero.

P62H-MCMP-EL-031.stem: Refer to the graph. If the short-run outcome shown persists initially, what market adjustment is most consistent with monopolistic competition?

choices.A: Exit shifts each incumbent firm’s demand right until price equals marginal cost
choices.B: Entry shifts each incumbent firm’s marginal cost downward until price equals ATC
choices.C: Entry shifts each incumbent firm’s demand left until economic profit is eliminated
choices.D: No entry occurs because differentiated firms can earn permanent economic profit

P62H-MCMP-EL-031.correct_answer: Entry shifts each incumbent firm’s demand left until economic profit is eliminated
P62H-MCMP-EL-031.feedback: Positive short-run profit attracts entry, which reduces the demand faced by each incumbent.

P62H-MCMP-EL-032.stem: Refer to the graph. Which feature most directly shows allocative inefficiency at the firm’s chosen output?

choices.A: Price of $37 exceeds ATC of $33 by $4
choices.B: ATC of $33 exceeds marginal cost of $23 by $10
choices.C: MR equals MC at $23 when quantity equals 50
choices.D: Price of $37 exceeds marginal cost of $23

P62H-MCMP-EL-032.correct_answer: Price of $37 exceeds marginal cost of $23
P62H-MCMP-EL-032.feedback: Allocative efficiency requires P = MC; here P exceeds MC by $14.

P62H-MCMP-EL-033.stem: Refer to the graph. If the zero-profit outcome shown is a long-run equilibrium, what market force has already done its work?

choices.A: Advertising has shifted firm demand until price equals marginal cost
choices.B: A regulator has set price equal to average total cost at Q = 36
choices.C: Collusion has eliminated rivalry and guaranteed zero economic profit
choices.D: Entry or exit has adjusted firm demand until economic profit is zero

P62H-MCMP-EL-033.correct_answer: Entry or exit has adjusted firm demand until economic profit is zero
P62H-MCMP-EL-033.feedback: Long-run entry and exit shift each firm’s demand until P = ATC at the chosen output.

P62H-MCMP-EL-034.stem: Refer to the graph. Which statement best captures the two inefficiencies shown?

choices.A: The firm has P < MC and produces above the minimum-ATC quantity
choices.B: The firm has P = MC but ATC exceeds price
choices.C: The firm has P > MC and produces below the minimum-ATC quantity
choices.D: The firm has MR = demand and produces at minimum ATC

P62H-MCMP-EL-034.correct_answer: The firm has P > MC and produces below the minimum-ATC quantity
P62H-MCMP-EL-034.feedback: P > MC indicates allocative inefficiency, and Q = 36 below efficient scale Q = 50 indicates productive inefficiency.

P62H-MCMP-EL-035.stem: Refer to the graph. Compared with a profitable short-run position, what happened to the demand facing the incumbent as entry occurred?

choices.A: It became perfectly horizontal at the quantity where ATC is minimized
choices.B: It shifted outward until the firm produced where price equals marginal cost
choices.C: It became identical to marginal revenue throughout the relevant output range
choices.D: It shifted inward until it became tangent to ATC at the chosen output

P62H-MCMP-EL-035.correct_answer: It shifted inward until it became tangent to ATC at the chosen output
P62H-MCMP-EL-035.feedback: Entry reduces each incumbent’s demand until the firm earns zero economic profit.

P62H-MCMP-EL-036.stem: Refer to the graph. The firm could lower ATC by producing 50 units. Why is that not necessarily profit maximizing?

choices.A: MR no longer equals MC at Q = 50 under the current demand curve
choices.B: ATC cannot decline when a monopolistically competitive firm expands output
choices.C: Producing 50 units would eliminate the firm’s product differentiation
choices.D: Long-run equilibrium requires the firm to maximize use of physical capacity

P62H-MCMP-EL-036.correct_answer: MR no longer equals MC at Q = 50 under the current demand curve
P62H-MCMP-EL-036.feedback: Minimum ATC is not the firm’s objective; profit maximization still follows MR = MC.

P62H-MCMP-EL-037.stem: Refer to the displayed long-run firm graph. A policymaker argues that because entry has eliminated economic profit, consumers cannot gain from additional mutually beneficial trades. Which response is economically sound?

choices.A: P = ATC proves P = MC, so the policymaker’s inference is sound
choices.B: P = ATC establishes zero profit, but P > MC still signals a markup; a policy must also consider differentiated-product benefits and cost recovery
choices.C: The firm must earn positive economic profit because output is below minimum ATC
choices.D: Free entry makes the firm a price taker, so the plotted downward-sloping demand is irrelevant

P62H-MCMP-EL-037.correct_answer: P = ATC establishes zero profit, but P > MC still signals a markup; a policy must also consider differentiated-product benefits and cost recovery
P62H-MCMP-EL-037.feedback: The graph combines P = ATC with P > MC and output below efficient scale. Entry removes profit without eliminating markup. The markup identifies a potential allocative issue, but the graph does not quantify the value of variety or the costs of a proposed remedy.

P62H-MCMP-H-013.stem: Refer to the graph. Demand is tangent to ATC at Q1 = 20 and price $70. Which combination is correct?

choices.A: Zero economic profit, positive markup, and excess capacity
choices.B: Positive economic profit with production at minimum average total cost and price equal to marginal cost
choices.C: Zero markup and allocative efficiency
choices.D: Economic loss and immediate exit

P62H-MCMP-H-013.correct_answer: Zero economic profit, positive markup, and excess capacity
P62H-MCMP-H-013.feedback: Tangency gives P=ATC, while P>MC and Q is below minimum ATC.

P62H-MCMP-H-014.stem: Refer to the graph. Suppose the firm’s demand shifts outward while costs are unchanged. What is the immediate short-run effect?

choices.A: The firm must earn zero profit immediately
choices.B: The firm can earn economic profit, encouraging entry
choices.C: Existing-firm demand shifts left immediately because entry occurs before the outward demand change
choices.D: The minimum-ATC quantity falls automatically

P62H-MCMP-H-014.correct_answer: The firm can earn economic profit, encouraging entry
P62H-MCMP-H-014.feedback: An outward demand shift can create short-run profit before entry responds.

P62H-MCMP-H-015.stem: Refer to the graph. Which equality at Q1 establishes that the firm earns zero economic profit?

choices.A: Price equals average total cost
choices.B: Price equals marginal cost
choices.C: Marginal revenue equals average total cost
choices.D: Average total cost equals minimum average variable cost

P62H-MCMP-H-015.feedback: The demand curve is tangent to ATC at Q1, so price equals average total cost and economic profit is zero.

P62H-MCMP-H-016.stem: Refer to the graph. After short-run profit induces entry, what happens to the demand curve facing an existing firm?

choices.A: It shifts left until it is tangent to ATC
choices.B: It shifts right until price equals marginal cost
choices.C: It becomes horizontal at minimum ATC
choices.D: It remains fixed while marginal cost shifts left

P62H-MCMP-H-016.correct_answer: It shifts left until it is tangent to ATC
P62H-MCMP-H-016.feedback: Entry provides more substitutes and shifts each existing firm’s demand left until tangency restores zero economic profit.

P62H-MCMP-H-017.stem: Refer to the graph. Which comparison at Q1 demonstrates allocative inefficiency?

choices.A: Price exceeds marginal cost
choices.B: Price equals marginal cost
choices.C: Price is below average variable cost
choices.D: Marginal revenue exceeds price

P62H-MCMP-H-017.feedback: At Q1 the demand curve gives price above marginal cost, so the allocative-efficiency condition P = MC is not met.

P62H-MCMP-H-018.stem: Refer to the graph. Once entry restores long-run equilibrium, which combination can still persist?

choices.A: Zero economic profit with a positive markup
choices.B: Positive economic profit with price equal to marginal cost
choices.C: A shutdown loss with minimum average total cost
choices.D: Zero economic profit with no excess capacity

P62H-MCMP-H-018.correct_answer: Zero economic profit with a positive markup
P62H-MCMP-H-018.feedback: Tangency gives zero economic profit, while the downward-sloping demand curve leaves price above marginal cost.

P62H-MCMP-H-019.stem: Refer to the graph. Q2 marks minimum ATC while the firm produces Q1. What does Q2 − Q1 measure?

choices.A: Excess capacity
choices.B: Economic profit
choices.C: The price markup
choices.D: The shutdown gap

P62H-MCMP-H-019.feedback: Excess capacity is the difference between efficient-scale output at minimum ATC and the firm’s profit-maximizing output.

P62H-MCMP-H-020.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does entry stop at the long-run outcome shown?

choices.A: Price equals average total cost, so economic profit is zero
choices.B: Price equals marginal cost, so allocative efficiency is achieved
choices.C: Output equals efficient scale, so excess capacity is zero
choices.D: Average variable cost equals zero, so shutdown is impossible

P62H-MCMP-H-020.correct_answer: Price equals average total cost, so economic profit is zero
P62H-MCMP-H-020.feedback: Entry stops when the demand curve is tangent to ATC and price equals ATC, eliminating economic profit.

P62H-MCMP-H-021.stem: A costly brand campaign shifts demand right but also makes demand less elastic. Which conclusion is safest?

choices.A: Output, price, and profit effects depend on both the demand change and campaign cost
choices.B: Profit must rise
choices.C: Price must fall
choices.D: Marginal cost must remain above marginal revenue at every possible quantity after the campaign

P62H-MCMP-H-021.correct_answer: Output, price, and profit effects depend on both the demand change and campaign cost
P62H-MCMP-H-021.feedback: Demand and cost effects must be evaluated together.

P62H-MCMP-H-032.stem: Refer to the graph. Why is the firm’s price read from the demand curve rather than from the MR = MC intersection?

choices.A: Price is read from demand after output is chosen where MR = MC
choices.B: Price must equal marginal cost at the profit-maximizing output
choices.C: The firm chooses price where ATC intersects marginal cost
choices.D: The $23 value is the price consumers pay on the demand curve

P62H-MCMP-H-032.correct_answer: Price is read from demand after output is chosen where MR = MC
P62H-MCMP-H-032.feedback: For a downward-sloping demand curve, the firm chooses Q where MR = MC and then reads price from demand.

P62H-MCMP-H-034.stem: Refer to the graph. Why is zero economic profit consistent with the firm continuing to operate?

choices.A: Revenue covers all explicit and implicit economic costs
choices.B: Zero economic profit means the firm receives no revenue
choices.C: The firm continues only because price equals marginal cost
choices.D: The firm must be subsidized whenever economic profit is zero

P62H-MCMP-H-034.correct_answer: Revenue covers all explicit and implicit economic costs
P62H-MCMP-H-034.feedback: P = ATC means the firm covers all economic costs, including normal return.

P62H-MCMP-H-036.stem: Refer to the graph. Which statement best distinguishes the displayed outcome from a perfectly competitive long-run equilibrium?

choices.A: A competitive firm also faces a downward-sloping demand curve
choices.B: A competitive firm sets MR below price at its chosen output
choices.C: The firm can have P = ATC while still having P > MC
choices.D: Perfect competition requires economic profit to remain positive

P62H-MCMP-H-036.correct_answer: The firm can have P = ATC while still having P > MC
P62H-MCMP-H-036.feedback: Monopolistic competition can have zero economic profit with a markup because firm demand slopes downward.

P62H-MCMP-H-037.stem: Refer to the graph. Why does the firm not expand from Q = 36 to the efficient scale of Q = 50?

choices.A: The firm is physically unable to produce more than 36 units
choices.B: Price would rise automatically if output increased to 50
choices.C: Marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost at every output above 36
choices.D: Profit maximization is governed by MR = MC, not by minimizing ATC alone

P62H-MCMP-H-037.correct_answer: Profit maximization is governed by MR = MC, not by minimizing ATC alone
P62H-MCMP-H-037.feedback: The firm stops at MR = MC even though ATC would be lower at a larger output.

P62H-MCMP-H-038.stem: Refer to the graph. Which pair of facts demonstrates long-run zero economic profit and productive inefficiency?

choices.A: P = ATC at Q = 36, while minimum ATC occurs at Q = 50
choices.B: P = MC at Q = 36, while ATC is constant after Q = 50
choices.C: MR = demand at Q = 36, while MC is minimized at Q = 50
choices.D: P exceeds ATC at Q = 36, while MR equals zero at Q = 50

P62H-MCMP-H-038.correct_answer: P = ATC at Q = 36, while minimum ATC occurs at Q = 50
P62H-MCMP-H-038.feedback: P = ATC gives zero economic profit, while Q below the minimum-ATC output creates excess capacity.

P62H-MCMP-H-039.stem: Refer to the graph. Why is the long-run outcome not allocatively efficient?

choices.A: Price of $27 equals ATC at the chosen quantity of 36
choices.B: Price of $27 exceeds marginal cost of $15.50 at Q = 36
choices.C: ATC reaches its minimum of $25 at the efficient scale of 50
choices.D: Demand is tangent to ATC at the long-run quantity of 36

P62H-MCMP-H-039.correct_answer: Price of $27 exceeds marginal cost of $15.50 at Q = 36
P62H-MCMP-H-039.feedback: Allocative efficiency requires P = MC, but here price exceeds marginal cost by $11.50.

P62H-MCMP-L-032.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=20, minimum-ATC output Q2=34.64, price $70.00 and MC=$50.00. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $50.00; excess capacity 20 units.
choices.B: Markup $20.00; excess capacity 34.64 units.
choices.C: Markup $70.00; excess capacity 14.64 units.
choices.D: Markup $20.00; excess capacity 14.64 units.

P62H-MCMP-L-032.feedback: Markup is P−MC=70.00−50.00=$20.00. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=34.64−20=14.64 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-L-035.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=24, minimum-ATC output Q2=42.93, price $76.00 and MC=$49.60. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $49.60; excess capacity 24 units.
choices.B: Markup $26.40; excess capacity 42.93 units.
choices.C: Markup $26.40; excess capacity 18.93 units.
choices.D: Markup $76.00; excess capacity 18.93 units.

P62H-MCMP-L-035.feedback: Markup is P−MC=76.00−49.60=$26.40. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=42.93−24=18.93 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-L-038.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=18, minimum-ATC output Q2=30.12, price $64.00 and MC=$47.80. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $47.80; excess capacity 18 units.
choices.B: Markup $16.20; excess capacity 12.12 units.
choices.C: Markup $16.20; excess capacity 30.12 units.
choices.D: Markup $64.00; excess capacity 12.12 units.

P62H-MCMP-L-038.feedback: Markup is P−MC=64.00−47.80=$16.20. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=30.12−18=12.12 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-L-041.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=28, minimum-ATC output Q2=51.63, price $82.00 and MC=$48.40. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $33.60; excess capacity 23.63 units.
choices.B: Markup $48.40; excess capacity 28 units.
choices.C: Markup $33.60; excess capacity 51.63 units.
choices.D: Markup $82.00; excess capacity 23.63 units.

P62H-MCMP-L-041.feedback: Markup is P−MC=82.00−48.40=$33.60. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=51.63−28=23.63 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-L-044.stem: A long-run monopolistically competitive firm has chosen output Q1=22, minimum-ATC output Q2=35.47, price $68.00 and MC=$50.40. Using the displayed values, what are its markup and excess capacity?

choices.A: Markup $50.40; excess capacity 22 units.
choices.B: Markup $17.60; excess capacity 35.47 units.
choices.C: Markup $68.00; excess capacity 13.47 units.
choices.D: Markup $17.60; excess capacity 13.47 units.

P62H-MCMP-L-044.feedback: Markup is P−MC=68.00−50.40=$17.60. Excess capacity is Q2−Q1=35.47−22=13.47 units, using the displayed minimum-ATC output.

P62H-MCMP-L-091.stem: Refer to the graph. If entry eliminates the short-run profit shown while the firm remains monopolistically competitive, which long-run condition should emerge?

choices.A: Demand becomes tangent to ATC at the new MR = MC output
choices.B: Demand becomes horizontal at minimum ATC
choices.C: MR becomes identical to demand at every output
choices.D: Price falls below AVC so every incumbent shuts down

P62H-MCMP-L-091.correct_answer: Demand becomes tangent to ATC at the new MR = MC output
P62H-MCMP-L-091.feedback: Long-run entry shifts the firm’s demand until P = ATC at the profit-maximizing quantity while demand remains downward sloping.

P62H-MCMP-L-092.stem: Refer to the graph. Which statement best evaluates the claim that zero economic profit makes the firm both productively and allocatively efficient?

choices.A: Zero profit alone proves neither minimum ATC production nor P = MC
choices.B: The student is correct whenever P equals ATC
choices.C: Only productive efficiency fails; allocative efficiency follows from zero profit
choices.D: Only allocative efficiency fails; productive efficiency follows from zero profit

P62H-MCMP-L-092.correct_answer: Zero profit alone proves neither minimum ATC production nor P = MC
P62H-MCMP-L-092.feedback: Zero economic profit is not an efficiency test. The graph still has a downward-sloping demand curve and P > MC.

P62H-MCMP-L-093.stem: Refer to the graph. Suppose a policy forced price down to marginal cost at Q = 36 without changing costs. What tension would arise?

choices.A: Economic profit would rise because price would equal marginal cost
choices.B: ATC would automatically fall to $15.50 at Q = 36
choices.C: The firm would no longer cover the $27 ATC shown at that output
choices.D: Excess capacity would disappear because Q would remain 36

P62H-MCMP-L-093.correct_answer: The firm would no longer cover the $27 ATC shown at that output
P62H-MCMP-L-093.feedback: At Q = 36, MC is $15.50 while ATC and current price are $27; forcing P to MC would put price below ATC.

P62H-MCMP-L-094.stem: Refer to the graph. After short-run profit attracts entry, which sequence correctly describes the adjustment toward long-run equilibrium?

choices.A: Entry shifts incumbent demand outward; markup disappears; output reaches minimum ATC
choices.B: Entry lowers marginal cost; demand becomes horizontal; positive profit remains
choices.C: Entry raises average total cost; price falls below AVC; all incumbents exit
choices.D: Entry shifts incumbent demand inward; profit falls to zero; output stays below minimum ATC

P62H-MCMP-L-094.correct_answer: Entry shifts incumbent demand inward; profit falls to zero; output stays below minimum ATC
P62H-MCMP-L-094.feedback: Entry shifts each incumbent’s demand inward until zero profit, while product differentiation leaves a downward-sloping demand curve and excess capacity.

P62H-MCMP-L-095.stem: Refer to the long-run monopolistic-competition graph. A proposal would force each firm to produce at minimum ATC while also pricing at MC. Which assessment uses the diagram and recognizes what it cannot establish about welfare?

choices.A: The current markup is $11.50 and excess capacity is 14 units; policy evaluation must also weigh lost variety and cost recovery, which the firm diagram does not measure
choices.B: The current $11.50 markup is economic profit, so eliminating it necessarily leaves every variety financially viable
choices.C: Current zero profit proves efficient output, so neither the markup nor product variety belongs in welfare analysis
choices.D: Excess capacity is 14 units of unsold inventory, so ordering its sale necessarily raises total consumer welfare

P62H-MCMP-L-095.correct_answer: The current markup is $11.50 and excess capacity is 14 units; policy evaluation must also weigh lost variety and cost recovery, which the firm diagram does not measure
P62H-MCMP-L-095.feedback: At Q = 36, P = ATC = $27 while MC = $15.50, giving an $11.50 markup. Minimum ATC occurs at Q = 50, so excess capacity is 14 units, not inventory. Producing more at a mandated price is not automatically feasible at zero profit. Buyers may value differentiation; the diagram alone cannot quantify the benefits of variety or the policy’s net welfare effect.

P62I-OLI-EL-007.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. After identifying both firms’ best responses, which pure-strategy Nash equilibrium follows?

choices.A: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column Y
choices.B: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column X
choices.C: Row A, Column Y; Row B, Column X
choices.D: Row A, Column Y; Row B, Column Y

P62I-OLI-EL-007.correct_answer: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column Y
P62I-OLI-EL-007.feedback: Trace both players’ best responses; only mutual best responses are Nash equilibria.

P62I-OLI-H-010.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. Which statement about the Row firm’s dominant strategy is correct?

choices.A: A
choices.B: B
choices.C: Both row strategies are dominant
choices.D: The joint-payoff-maximizing cell

P62I-OLI-H-010.feedback: Compare Row’s two payoffs separately under each Column strategy.

P62I-OLI-H-012.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. With payoffs ordered (Row, Column), which cell is a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium?

choices.A: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column X
choices.B: Row A, Column Y; Row B, Column X
choices.C: Row A, Column Y; Row B, Column Y
choices.D: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column Y

P62I-OLI-H-012.correct_answer: Row A, Column X; Row B, Column Y
P62I-OLI-H-012.feedback: A Nash equilibrium is a cell containing mutual best responses.

P62I-OLI-H-013.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. Which statement about the Row firm’s dominant strategy is correct?

choices.A: B
choices.B: A
choices.C: Both row strategies are dominant
choices.D: The joint-payoff-maximizing cell

P62I-OLI-H-013.feedback: Compare Row’s two payoffs separately under each Column strategy.

P62I-OLI-H-016.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. Which statement about the Row firm’s dominant strategy is correct?

choices.A: A
choices.B: Both row strategies are dominant
choices.C: The joint-payoff-maximizing cell
choices.D: Row has no strictly dominant strategy

P62I-OLI-H-016.correct_answer: Row has no strictly dominant strategy
P62I-OLI-H-016.feedback: Compare Row’s two payoffs separately under each Column strategy.

P62I-OLI-H-018.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. With payoffs ordered (Row, Column), which cell is a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium?

choices.A: Row A, Column X; Row A, Column Y; Row B, Column X; Row B, Column Y
choices.B: No pure-strategy Nash equilibrium
choices.C: Row A, Column Y
choices.D: Row B, Column X

P62I-OLI-H-018.feedback: A Nash equilibrium is a cell containing mutual best responses.

P62I-OLI-H-019.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix. Which statement about the Row firm’s dominant strategy is correct?

choices.A: A
choices.B: Both row strategies are dominant
choices.C: B
choices.D: The joint-payoff-maximizing cell

P62I-OLI-H-019.feedback: Compare Row’s two payoffs separately under each Column strategy.

P62I-OLI-L-004.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix for a port-services coordination review. Payoffs are profits ordered (Row, Column). Comparing both players’ best responses with the sum of their payoffs, which conclusion is supported?

choices.A: B/Y is the only pure equilibrium because Column prefers its payoff there
choices.B: A/X is the only pure equilibrium because it has the largest joint total
choices.C: Neither diagonal cell is an equilibrium because the off-diagonal totals are lower
choices.D: A/X and B/Y are pure equilibria; A/X has the larger joint total, 23 versus 21

P62I-OLI-L-004.correct_answer: A/X and B/Y are pure equilibria; A/X has the larger joint total, 23 versus 21
P62I-OLI-L-004.feedback: Against X, Row chooses A; against Y, Row chooses B. Against A, Column chooses X; against B, Column chooses Y. Both diagonal cells are equilibria, with joint totals 23 and 21. Neither player has a dominant strategy. The maximum joint-profit cell is also one equilibrium; it need not be the selected outcome.

P62I-OLI-L-010.stem: Refer to the payoff matrix for a rotating delivery-slot game. Payoffs are profits ordered (Row, Column). Comparing both players’ best responses with the sum of their payoffs, which conclusion is supported?

choices.A: There are four pure-strategy equilibria because all four joint totals equal 8
choices.B: There is no pure-strategy equilibrium; all four cells tie at a joint total of 8
choices.C: A/X is the unique equilibrium because Row receives 6 there
choices.D: B/Y is the joint optimum because Column receives 2 there

P62I-OLI-L-010.correct_answer: There is no pure-strategy equilibrium; all four cells tie at a joint total of 8
P62I-OLI-L-010.feedback: Row chooses A against X and B against Y. Column chooses Y against A and X against B. Every pure cell permits a profitable deviation. Each cell totals 8, so equal joint profit does not create a pure equilibrium. A mixed-strategy equilibrium is distinct from a pure one.

P62I-OLI-L-072.stem: Two rival cruise lines keep fares at $72 and sell 30 units each in the kinked-demand model shown. Rivals match fare cuts but do not match fare increases. A per-unit cost increase raises this firm’s constant MC from $48 to $54, with demand and fixed cost unchanged. How do its profit-maximizing fare, quantity and economic profit change?

choices.A: Fare rises to $78 and quantity stays at 30; economic profit is unchanged.
choices.B: Fare and quantity stay at $72 and 30; economic profit is unchanged because MR has a gap.
choices.C: Fare falls and quantity rises; economic profit falls by less than $180.
choices.D: Fare and quantity stay at $72 and 30; economic profit falls by $180.

P62I-OLI-L-072.correct_answer: Fare and quantity stay at $72 and 30; economic profit falls by $180.
P62I-OLI-L-072.feedback: At Q=30 the MR gap runs from $36 to $60. Both MC=$48 and MC=$54 fall inside it, so the optimum remains at the kink, P=$72 and Q=30. Cost rises $6 on each of 30 units, lowering profit by $180.

P62I-OLI-L-073.stem: A firm faces the kinked demand shown: P=70−0.5Q up to Q=20 and P=90−1.5Q above Q=20. Its constant MC initially equals $40. Compare a rise in MC to $45 with a rise to $55, holding demand fixed. Which conclusion is correct?

choices.A: At MC=$45 the firm keeps Q=20 and P=$60; at MC=$55 it reduces output to Q=15 and raises price to $62.50.
choices.B: At MC=$45 and MC=$55 the firm keeps Q=20 and P=$60 because any cost change lies inside the MR gap.
choices.C: At MC=$45 the firm keeps Q=20 and P=$60; at MC=$55 it expands output to Q=25 and lowers price to $52.50.
choices.D: At MC=$45 it reduces output to Q=15 and raises price to $62.50; at MC=$55 it returns to Q=20 and P=$60.

P62I-OLI-L-073.correct_answer: At MC=$45 the firm keeps Q=20 and P=$60; at MC=$55 it reduces output to Q=15 and raises price to $62.50.
P62I-OLI-L-073.feedback: At the kink MR drops from $50 to $30. MC=$45 lies within that range, but MC=$55 lies above it. On the upper demand branch MR=70−Q, so 70−Q=55 gives Q=15 and P=70−0.5×15=$62.50.

P62I-OLI-L-074.stem: A firm faces the kinked demand shown, with prevailing price $72, quantity 30 and constant MC=$48. An input improvement lowers MC to $42, while a recurring license fee adds $300 to fixed cost. Demand does not change. Which evaluation correctly separates the output decision from the profit effect?

choices.A: Price and quantity stay at the kink; the $180 variable-cost saving exceeds the $300 fee, so economic profit rises by $120.
choices.B: Price and quantity stay at the kink; the $180 variable-cost saving is smaller than the $300 fee, so economic profit falls by $120.
choices.C: The fixed fee raises MC above the MR gap, so quantity falls; the variable-cost saving cannot affect profit.
choices.D: The lower MC moves quantity above the kink; the fixed fee is a variable cost, so profit is unchanged.

P62I-OLI-L-074.correct_answer: Price and quantity stay at the kink; the $180 variable-cost saving is smaller than the $300 fee, so economic profit falls by $120.
P62I-OLI-L-074.feedback: The MR gap at Q=30 is $36 to $60; MC=$42 remains inside it, so P and Q stay at $72 and 30. Variable cost falls by ($48−$42)×30=$180. The $300 fixed fee does not enter MC but exceeds that saving, reducing profit by $120.

P62I-OLI-LB-007.stem: Use the displayed payoff matrix as the baseline. A coordination program adds 6 to each firm’s payoff only at (A,X), leaving all other cells unchanged. Which list contains all pure-strategy Nash equilibria after the change, and which outcome maximizes joint payoff?

choices.A: Both (A,X) and (B,Y) are equilibria; (A,X) maximizes joint payoff at 32.
choices.B: Only (A,X) is an equilibrium; improving that cell removes the incentive to choose B against Y.
choices.C: Only (B,Y) is an equilibrium; the added payoff cannot alter any best response.
choices.D: Both (A,Y) and (B,X) are equilibria; their unequal payoffs maximize the joint total.

P62I-OLI-LB-007.correct_answer: Both (A,X) and (B,Y) are equilibria; (A,X) maximizes joint payoff at 32.
P62I-OLI-LB-007.feedback: The new (A,X) payoff is (16,16), so A is preferred to B against X and X to Y against A. Against Y, row still prefers B (7>5), and against B, column still prefers Y (7>5). Thus the old (B,Y) equilibrium also remains, while (A,X) yields the highest joint payoff.

P62I-OLI-LB-021.stem: Use the cartel graph with demand P=100−2Q and MC=$20. Two identical cartel members split the joint-profit-maximizing output equally. One secretly produces one additional unit while its rival holds its quota. Which comparison explains the incentive conflict?

choices.A: The deviator’s profit falls from $400 to $398, while combined profit rises from $800 to $818.
choices.B: Both member and joint profit rise because an extra unit always sells above marginal cost.
choices.C: The deviator’s profit rises from $400 to $418, while combined profit falls from $800 to $798.
choices.D: Neither profit changes because the original quota was jointly optimal.

P62I-OLI-LB-021.correct_answer: The deviator’s profit rises from $400 to $418, while combined profit falls from $800 to $798.
P62I-OLI-LB-021.feedback: Joint MR=100−4Q equals 20 at Q=20, P=60; each supplies 10 for profit $400. Deviation makes total Q=21 and P=58; the deviator earns (58−20)×11=$418. Combined profit is (58−20)×21=$798.

P62I-OLI-LB-024.stem: Use the cartel graph with demand P=140−2.5Q and MC=$30. Two members split cartel output equally. One adds two units while the other holds its quota. Which current-profit comparison and deterrence threshold are correct, ignoring other effects?

choices.A: The deviator loses $10 while combined profit gains $45; any positive punishment is unnecessary.
choices.B: The deviator gains $45 while combined profit falls $10; an expected present-value punishment greater than $45 deters this deviation.
choices.C: The deviator gains $110 and combined profit rises $110; a punishment below $45 is sufficient.
choices.D: The deviator gains $45 and combined profit is unchanged; joint optimization guarantees no harm to its rival.

P62I-OLI-LB-024.correct_answer: The deviator gains $45 while combined profit falls $10; an expected present-value punishment greater than $45 deters this deviation.
P62I-OLI-LB-024.feedback: Joint optimum is Q=22, P=85, with 11 units and $605 profit per member. Deviation gives total Q=24, P=80; the deviator supplies 13 for $650, a $45 gain. Total profit changes from $1210 to $1200. Compare the $45 gain with the discounted expected future penalty.

P62I-OLI-LB-027.stem: Use the cartel graph with demand P=100−2Q and MC=$20. Compare a $200 lump-sum license charge on the cartel with a $10 tax per unit. The cartel stays active and reoptimizes jointly. Which comparison is correct?

choices.A: The license leaves Q=20 and P=$60 with net profit $600; the per-unit tax gives Q=17.5 and P=$65 with net profit $612.50.
choices.B: Both policies leave Q=20 and P=$60 because all taxes are fixed costs.
choices.C: The license reduces output to 17.5, while the per-unit tax leaves output 20 because its payment is a transfer.
choices.D: Both policies increase output to 40 because taxes force price to equal the original MC.

P62I-OLI-LB-027.correct_answer: The license leaves Q=20 and P=$60 with net profit $600; the per-unit tax gives Q=17.5 and P=$65 with net profit $612.50.
P62I-OLI-LB-027.feedback: The license leaves MR=MC unchanged and subtracts $200 from original profit $800. The unit tax raises effective MC to $30: 100−4Q=30 gives Q=17.5 and P=65, with net operating profit (65−30)×17.5=$612.50.

PG1-SUP-L-001.stem: Refer to the graph. A producer says the move from A to B proves that supply increased by 125 thousand units. What is the correct diagnosis?

choices.A: Any quantity increase counts as an increase in supply.
choices.B: A and B show a leftward shift of the supply curve.
choices.C: The higher quantity means the demand curve shifted right.
choices.D: It is more quantity supplied, not an increase in supply.

PG1-SUP-L-001.correct_answer: It is more quantity supplied, not an increase in supply.
PG1-SUP-L-001.feedback: A change in the good's own price changes quantity supplied along a fixed supply curve. A supply increase would require a rightward shift of the entire curve.

PMC-COP-R-010.stem: A learner says, “If the owner did not write a check, the resource has no cost.

choices.A: Only variable resources have economic costs
choices.B: Every implicit cost must appear on an invoice
choices.C: Opportunity cost matters only for consumers
choices.D: Owner-supplied resources can have implicit opportunity costs even without a cash payment

PMC-COP-R-010.correct_answer: Owner-supplied resources can have implicit opportunity costs even without a cash payment
PMC-COP-R-010.feedback: Economic cost includes the value of the next-best use of owner-supplied resources.

PMC-COP-R-025.stem: A learner calls zero economic profit a “loss.

choices.A: Zero economic profit means all explicit and implicit costs, including normal profit, are covered
choices.B: Zero economic profit means revenue is zero
choices.C: Zero economic profit means explicit costs exceed revenue
choices.D: Zero economic profit excludes owner compensation

PMC-COP-R-025.correct_answer: Zero economic profit means all explicit and implicit costs, including normal profit, are covered
PMC-COP-R-025.feedback: Normal profit is included in economic cost, so zero economic profit can be a sustainable outcome.

PMC-COP-R-068.stem: A learner says AFC eventually rises because “all U-shaped costs rise.

choices.A: AFC rises whenever MC rises
choices.B: AFC keeps falling as fixed cost is spread over more output
choices.C: AFC is U-shaped like AVC
choices.D: AFC equals MC at its minimum

PMC-COP-R-068.correct_answer: AFC keeps falling as fixed cost is spread over more output
PMC-COP-R-068.feedback: AFC is not U-shaped in the standard model; it declines as quantity increases.

PMC-COP-R-117.stem: A learner says, “Fixed cost and sunk cost mean the same thing.

choices.A: A fixed cost can be avoidable in a future decision; a sunk cost is unrecoverable
choices.B: Every sunk cost varies with output
choices.C: Every fixed cost has already been paid forever
choices.D: Sunk costs are always implicit

PMC-COP-R-117.correct_answer: A fixed cost can be avoidable in a future decision; a sunk cost is unrecoverable
PMC-COP-R-117.feedback: Fixed describes how cost behaves with current output; sunk describes whether it can be recovered.

PMS-ELAS-R-029.stem: A learner says labor demand elasticity is unrelated to substitution possibilities. Best correction?

choices.A: More available substitutes for a type of labor generally make labor demand more elastic
choices.B: Substitutes make labor demand perfectly inelastic
choices.C: Factor demand elasticity depends only on worker preferences
choices.D: Substitution changes labor supply but never labor demand

PMS-ELAS-R-029.correct_answer: More available substitutes for a type of labor generally make labor demand more elastic
PMS-ELAS-R-029.feedback: Employers can respond more strongly to wage changes when alternative inputs are available.
